facts.fact: The NINAuth consent-based identity verification platform, launched by President Tinubu on 30 October 2025, processes 1.3 million verification requests daily, says NIMC's head of Software and Biometrics.
NINAuth verifies identity for banks, for remote customer onboarding, and for telecom operators' SIM registration, all major operators being integrated, says NIMC's head of Software and Biometrics.

NGA.note: Nothing on a link between the civil register and the ID system.
Only an upcoming card on the Central Bank's AfriGo scheme is mentioned, with no role over payments stated.
Nothing on consumer rules for digital finance.
Verification for subsidies and social programmes is mentioned, but no government payment to people is described.
126.7 million enrolled is stated but no population or share of it, so no cut is settled.
Nothing on a number at birth.
An IDEMIA upgrade partnership is named but who operates, maintains or owns the system is not stated.
No public register is said to be keyed on the national number.

facts.fact: 126.7 million Nigerians are enrolled in the National Identity Management System, each with an 11-digit National Identification Number, says NIMC's head of Software and Biometrics.

Banks and telecom operators verify people against the national ID through NINAuth, with 153 million SIM cards now linked to National Identification Numbers, says NIMC's head of Software and Biometrics.
NINAuth is used for remote bank customer verification and for telecom SIM registration, two sectors, says NIMC's head of Software and Biometrics.
NINAuth processes 1.3 million verification requests daily and 153 million SIM cards are linked to National Identification Numbers, says NIMC's head of Software and Biometrics.

NGA.note: Only an approximate 60 million adults lacking formal financial access, not a survey share.
Nothing on retail payment services in service.
Nothing on tax or fee payment.
